leads.title: Gender Recognition Act 2004
leads.documents: Allows transgender people to change legal gender in the UK, acquire new birth certificate and full recognition of acquired sex; requires evidence to Gender Recognition Panel, 2-year transition, GRC issuance; surgery not required but accepted as evidence; married trans people required to divorce/annul for GRC.
leads.detail: Cited as Gender Recognition Act 2004 (Welsh: Deddf Cydnabod Rhywedd 2004); in force since 4 April 2005

leads.title: Corbett v Corbett (1970)
leads.documents: Court decision that made it legally impossible for transgender people to change sex marker on birth certificate, rendering them unable to marry person of other gender; used as precedent including by US courts.
leads.detail: Cited as 1970 decision of the court case Corbett v Corbett

leads.title: Goodwin v United Kingdom (2002) - European Court of Human Rights
leads.documents: Found UK in breach of Articles 8 and 12 of the European Convention on Human Rights under Corbett status quo; ruling led to passing of Gender Recognition Act 2004.
leads.detail: Cited as 2002 European Court of Human Rights case Goodwin v United Kingdom, breach of Articles 8 and 12

leads.title: P v S and Cornwall County Council (1996) - European Court of Justice
leads.documents: Ruled that European anti-gender discrimination law applied to trans people, prior to Gender Recognition Act.
leads.detail: Cited as P v S and Cornwall County Council decided by the European Court of Justice in 1996

leads.title: Government Policy Concerning Transsexual People - Lord Chancellor's office
leads.documents: UK government policy document categorically stating transsexualism 'is not a mental illness.'
leads.detail: Published December 2002 by the Lord Chancellor's office

leads.title: Equality Act 2010
leads.documents: Extended discrimination protections for LGBT people to all areas; builds on protections in place since 1999.
leads.detail: Cited as Equality Act 2010 extending protections to all areas

leads.title: ILGA-Europe Review of LGBTI Rights - 2015, 2020, 2025 reports
leads.documents: Institutional human-rights ranking documenting backsliding: UK highest score in Europe in 2015 with 86% (92% Scotland), 9th place 66% in 2020 with concern about 'hostile climate on trans rights fuelled by opposition groups', 22nd place 45% in 2025, third steepest drop.
leads.detail: Cited as ILGA-Europe's 2015 review, 2020 ranking, and 2025 report

leads.title: Marriage (Same Sex Couples) Act 2013
leads.documents: Allows same-sex marriage in England and Wales, with full rights of civil marriage; no religious body compelled; Church of England and Church in Wales explicitly banned.
leads.detail: Passed July 2013, came into force 13 March 2014, first marriages 29 March 2014

leads.title: Civil Partnership Act 2004
leads.documents: First legal recognition of same-sex relationships in Britain; separate union giving most rights of civil marriage; can take place on approved premises and approved religious venues in England and Wales since 2011.
leads.detail: Passed 18 November 2004, came into effect 5 December 2005

leads.title: Office for National Statistics - 2024 survey
leads.documents: Government statistical report on sexual orientation: 4.8% of people in England and Wales identified as lesbian, gay, bisexual, or other; YouGov and Stonewall estimate 5-7% due to under-reporting.
leads.detail: Cited as 2024 survey from the Office for National Statistics for England and Wales
